title: The Past Tense (Preteritum)
goal: Form and use the Norwegian preteritum (simple past) of regular and common irregular verbs, and choose it when the time of an action is known.

objectives.statement: Form and use the Norwegian preteritum (simple past) of regular and common irregular verbs, and choose it when the time of an action is known.

spans.value: Maja and Jonas meet at work on Monday morning. Maja wants to know why Jonas did not answer his phone the previous evening.
Jeg jobbet til klokka fire. Så tok jeg bussen til sentrum og møtte Sara.

blocks.translation: I worked until four o’clock. Then I took the bus to the city centre and met Sara.
Did you go to the cinema?

spans.value: Nei, vi spiste på en liten restaurant. Etterpå gikk vi en tur.

blocks.translation: No, we ate at a small restaurant. Afterwards, we went for a walk.

spans.value: Jeg ringte deg klokka ni, men du svarte ikke.

blocks.translation: I called you at nine, but you didn’t answer.
Sorry. I didn’t see the phone.
I came home at eleven o’clock.

spans.value: The conversation has a clear past-time frame. Maja begins with i går, yesterday, and later mentions klokka ni, at nine o’clock. Jonas describes a sequence of events within that known period: he worked, took the bus, met Sara, ate, walked, and came home.
The verbs therefore appear in the simple past, called the

sections.title: Saying what happened at a known past time

spans.value: Use the preteritum when an action or state belongs to a known past time. The time may be stated directly:

en.value: She came home at ten o’clock.

spans.value: It may also be clear from the conversation. Once Maja has asked Hva gjorde du i går?, Jonas does not need to repeat i går in every answer. The shared context already establishes the time.

en.value: I took the bus to the city centre.

spans.value: The preteritum can describe actions, events, and states:
Compare the present tense with the preteritum:

no.value: Jonas jobber til klokka fire i dag.

en.value: Jonas works until four o’clock today.

no.value: Jonas jobbet til klokka fire i går.

en.value: Jonas worked until four o’clock yesterday.

no.value: Maja ringte Jonas klokka ni i går.

en.value: Maja called Jonas at nine yesterday.
They take the bus every Monday.
They took the bus last Monday.

spans.value: The time frame controls the choice. Nå and i dag can establish a present frame. I går, forrige mandag, and a past date establish a past frame.

statement.value: When the sentence describes what happened or was true at a stated or shared past time, put the verb in the preteritum.

sections.title: Forming the preteritum of regular verbs

spans.value: Many Norwegian verbs form the preteritum by adding an ending. These are
. Several common endings occur, so it is useful to learn an infinitive together with its past form.

no.value: Vi snakket med læreren etter timen.

en.value: We spoke with the teacher after class.

no.value: Bussen kom sent, så jeg ventet i tjue minutter.

en.value: The bus arrived late, so I waited for twenty minutes.

no.value: Sara kjøpte en kaffe på stasjonen.

en.value: Sara bought a coffee at the station.
Jonas met Sara in the city centre.

no.value: De spiste på en liten restaurant.

en.value: They ate at a small restaurant.

spans.value: Some verbs show a spelling adjustment as well as the ending. For example, å møte becomes møtte. Learn the written past form rather than adding letters mechanically.
Some regular verbs form the past with -de:

no.value: Familien levde i Oslo i mange år.

en.value: The family lived in Oslo for many years.

spans.value: Many short infinitives ending in a stressed vowel form the past with -dde:

en.value: to think or believe – thought or believed

no.value: Vi bodde nær sentrum i fjor.

en.value: We lived near the city centre last year.
I thought the restaurant was closed.
They reached the station at eight o’clock.

spans.value: These families help you notice patterns, but they do not let you predict every form with complete certainty. Record new verbs as pairs:
This is safer than remembering only the infinitive.
Norwegian past-tense verbs do not change according to the subject. The same form follows jeg, du, han, hun, vi, dere, and de.
This differs from English verbs such as was and were, but Norwegian still uses one preteritum form:
Do not add a new ending because the subject is plural.
Some frequent verbs do not form the preteritum with a predictable regular ending. These are
. Their past forms must be learned, but many occur so often that they soon become familiar.

en.value: to go or walk – went or walked
to get or receive – got or received
to leave or go – left or went
to become or remain – became or remained

spans.value: Several of these forms appear in the opening dialogue:

en.value: I came home at eleven o’clock.

no.value: Vi var på jobb til klokka fem.

en.value: We were at work until five o’clock.

no.value: Sara hadde en avtale i sentrum.

en.value: Sara had an appointment in the city centre.

no.value: Jeg fikk en melding fra Jonas.

en.value: I received a message from Jonas.
They went home after the film.

spans.value: A common mistake is to attach a regular ending to an irregular past form.

en.value: I walked home at ten o’clock.
I walked home at ten o’clock.

spans.value: The forms gikk and tok are already complete preteritum forms.

sections.title: Negatives and questions in the past

spans.value: The preteritum form remains on the main verb in negative statements.

en.value: I did not work on Sunday.
Maja did not call in the morning.
Jonas did not take the train.
They did not see the phone.

spans.value: Norwegian does not use an equivalent of English did not before another infinitive. Use the Norwegian past form directly:

en.value: I did not go to the cinema.

no.value: Jeg gjorde ikke gå på kino.

en.value: I did not go to the cinema.

spans.value: Questions also use the preteritum form directly, normally before the subject:
English uses did in these questions, but Norwegian does not add a separate past-tense helper. Jobbet, ringte, tok, and kom already express past time.

sections.title: Choosing the tense from the time frame

spans.value: Knowing a past form is not enough; you must also decide when to use it. Compare these pairs:

no.value: Sara går til jobb hver dag.

en.value: Sara walks to work every day.

no.value: Sara gikk til jobb i går.
Vi spiser middag klokka seks i dag.

en.value: We are eating dinner at six today.

no.value: Vi spiste middag klokka seks i går.

en.value: We ate dinner at six yesterday.

spans.value: Do not keep the present tense merely because the verb describes a habit in general. If the sentence refers to a particular known past occasion, use the preteritum.
The same applies when the time is established in a question:

en.value: What did you do on Saturday?

spans.value: The answer does not repeat på lørdag, but it remains within that past-time frame.
Later, Sara sends Maja a message and gives her version of the evening.

Jonas møtte meg ved stasjonen klokka fem. Først kjøpte vi kaffe. Så gikk vi til en restaurant og spiste middag. Jonas fikk en melding, men han så ikke på telefonen. Jeg dro hjem klokka halv ti, og Jonas tok bussen litt senere.

blocks.translation: Jonas met me at the station at five. First we bought coffee. Then we walked to a restaurant and ate dinner. Jonas received a message, but he did not look at his phone. I went home at half past nine, and Jonas took the bus a little later.

spans.value: Sara combines regular verbs and irregular verbs within one clear time frame.
The sequence words først, så, and litt senere organize the account, but the grammar stays simple: each event happened during the known past evening, so each verb is in the preteritum.

Imagine that a colleague asks what happened during a delayed journey yesterday. The situation may include leaving home, waiting for transport, taking another route, arriving late, and contacting someone.

prompt.value: Choose the meaning that fits the conversation.

options.text: «I går» beskriver en vanlig rutine, så «gikk» og «tok» uttrykker nåtid.
options.why: A routine reading conflicts with the specific past expression «i går».

options.text: Bare «gjorde» hører til fortiden; verbene i svaret har ingen etablert tidsramme.
options.why: The time frame established by the question also governs the answer.

options.text: «I går» etablerer en kjent fortid, og «gikk» og «tok» hører til den samme tidsrammen.
options.why: The question establishes one shared past-time frame for the reply.

text.value: «Jeg gikk til byen og tok bussen hjem.»

prompt.value: Fill in the forms that fit «i går».
Complete the story with the forms that fit «i går».
Maja wants to know whether Jonas took the train yesterday. Choose the negative yes/no question with «tok» and «ikke».

options.text: Tok ikke Jonas toget i går?
options.why: Tok is the preteritum form, and ikke makes this a negative question.

options.text: Tar ikke Jonas toget i går?
options.why: Tar is present tense and conflicts with «i går».

options.text: Tok Jonas toget i går?
options.why: This is a positive question, not a negative question.

options.text: Jonas tok ikke toget i går.
options.why: This is a negative statement, not a question.

prompt.value: Choose the verb form that fits the conversation.

options.text: er
options.why: Present tense conflicts with the time frame established by «i går».

options.text: var
options.why: The question places Jonas’s reply within yesterday’s known past time.

prompt.value: To Eva: Tell her what Lea did yesterday afternoon. Write a message and include these points in order: wait for the train until four; buy coffee; meet the neighbor at the station; eat lunch together; walk to the bus stop; get home at seven.

payload.judge_prompt: Report a verdict for each criterion id. Determine the overall pass from all criteria.

criteria.instruction: The response is a message to Eva that reports what happened during the afternoon.
The response includes all six supplied events without contradicting the facts.
The six events appear in the supplied chronological order.
The message is intelligible Norwegian.
The response reports the supplied train-waiting event with a natural preteritum form, for example «ventet»; accept equivalent natural past-tense wording.

The response reports the supplied buying, meeting, eating, walking, and arriving events with natural preteritum forms, for example «kjøpte», «møtte», «spiste», «gikk», and «kom»; accept equivalent natural past-tense wording.
The account maintains preteritum after the past time is established.

prompt.value: You arrived late for work yesterday. Write a connected message in Norwegian to a colleague and explain why you were late. Include these points in order: miss the bus at 7:10; ask a station worker about another route; take the train at eight; send your colleague a message; arrive at work at nine.

explanation.value: Fortell om hendelsene som ble avsluttet i går, med naturlige norske formuleringer.

payload.judge_prompt: Judge whether the message explains the delayed journey using the supplied events, in a coherent order, with completed events expressed in appropriate Norwegian past forms. Accept natural paraphrases.

criteria.instruction: Writes a connected message to a colleague explaining the late arrival yesterday.
Includes missing the 07:10 bus, asking a station employee for another route, changing to the 08:00 train, sending a message to the colleague, and arriving at work at 9:00, in that order.
Expresses the completed events with appropriate Norwegian past-tense forms; accept natural alternatives for the verbs and phrasing.

prompt.value: To Maja: Write a message about what you did at home last night. Include these events: make soup, call your sister, eat with her, and clean the kitchen.

payload.judge_prompt: Report a verdict for each criterion id. Determine the overall pass only if all criteria are satisfied.

criteria.instruction: The response is a message to Maja describing what happened at home yesterday evening.
The response includes making soup, calling the sister, eating together, and cleaning the kitchen without contradicting them.
The message is intelligible Norwegian.
The cooking, calling, and cleaning events use appropriate regular preteritum forms.
The eating event uses the appropriate preteritum form «spiste».
The verbs remain compatible with the established time «i går» and use past tense.

prompt.value: Choose the verb pair that fits both time frames.

options.text: jobbet — ringer
options.why: This reverses the tense choices licensed by «hver mandag» and «i går».

options.text: jobber — ringer
options.why: The second form ignores the stated past time.

options.text: jobbet — ringte
options.why: The first form treats a current recurring routine as a finished past occasion.

options.text: jobber — ringte
options.why: The recurring present situation and the specific past event require different tenses.

options.text: Liv plantet tulipanløk i går. Kaja og Ali planter samme type løk senere på ettermiddagen.
options.why: Planter changes the second action to present even though the note places it yesterday.

options.text: Liv plantet tulipanløk i går. Kaja og Ali plantet samme type løk senere på ettermiddagen.
options.why: Plantet stays the same with Liv and with the plural subject Kaja og Ali.

options.text: Liv planter tulipanløk i går. Kaja og Ali plantet samme type løk senere på ettermiddagen.

options.text: Går du på kino på lørdag?
options.why: This asks about a present or planned event rather than the completed Saturday event.

options.text: Gikk du på kino på lørdag?
options.why: Norwegian places the complete past-tense verb before the subject.

options.text: Gjorde du gå på kino på lørdag?

prompt.value: Choose the message where only the verb tenses have been corrected.

options.text: I går jobbet jeg til fire. Etterpå gikk jeg hjem og spiser middag.
options.why: The final event is incorrectly shifted into present tense.

options.text: I dag jobber jeg til fire. Etterpå går jeg hjem og spiser middag.
options.why: This removes the errors by changing the message from yesterday to today.

options.text: I går jobbet jeg til fire. Etterpå gikk jeg hjem og spiste middag.
options.why: All three events belong to the same completed day.

options.text: I går jobbet jeg til fire. Etterpå går jeg hjem og spiste middag.

prompt.value: Choose the sentence with the correct past-tense forms.

options.text: I går snakket Sara med Maja, og de kjøpe billetter.
options.why: The infinitive kjøpe is not a finite past form.

options.text: I går snakket Sara med Maja, og de kjøpte billetter.
options.why: Regular preteritum adds -et or -te to these verb stems.

prompt.value: Choose the sentence with the correct irregular past-tense forms.

options.text: I går går Mina til parken, tar en kaffe og kommer tilbake før middag.
options.why: These present forms conflict with the past time «i går».

options.text: I går gikkte Mina til parken, tokte en kaffe og komte tilbake før middag.
options.why: Irregular verbs do not take the regular -te ending.

options.text: I går gikk Mina til parken, tok en kaffe og kom tilbake før middag.
options.why: Gikk, tok, and kom are the correct irregular preteritum forms.
